name: survey-ore-vein-visibility
description: Validates ore vein visibility: run surveys at positions where ore is expected, then verify the overlay shows ore indicators. After a blast, check that ore vein markers are still visible or updated based on new terrain geometry. Requires the survey overlay to be wired into syncFromContext(). Former Finding #16 (with a single surveyor and 4 survey PendingActions queued back to back, one used to silently vanish from pendingActions without ever producing a SurveyResult) is resolved by #549: interruptActiveAction now correctly requeues an interrupted survey instead of losing it, so throughput is just slower (interruption/rest cost real ticks) -- a direct engine trace confirms all 5 of this file's survey PendingActions (4 seismic + 1 core_sample) do eventually complete, given enough ticks (by cumulative tick ~161). The file's mid-run checkpoint (after ~124 ticks) still asserts only 4 of 5 complete, matching that slower-but-complete throughput; the final checkpoint now falls past tick ~161 (the #553 drilling block below pushes well beyond it) and asserts all 5. #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file also hires a driller, buys a drill_rig, and ticks through the drill plan before charging/blasting -- cash bumped to $200,000 (campaign start) to survive a random lawsuit event (seed 42 deterministic, up to -$80,000) hit during that block, same fix as survey-overlay-lifecycle.json.

steps.description: #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, and this file's own tick blocks (surveys, then drilling) run long enough to roll a random event that can cost up to $80,000 (lawsuit_class_action_mega, seed 42 deterministic) -- the default $50,000 start plus survey/hire costs leaves too thin a cushion, so this mirrors survey-overlay-lifecycle.json's own cash:200000 bump (same seed, same event, same fix).

Test-only bootstrap, not a player action: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for the scenario's needs. No role tag -- there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

steps.description: #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. Employee #2 -- #1 is the surveyor hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:4 depth:6 start:15,15
steps.description: #553: confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles -- none drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm.

#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts). No staffed:true near-origin spawn here (campaign start), so this single driller/drill_rig takes real ticks to reach each hole. Sandbox-measured: all 4 holes land by cumulative +110 ticks post-drill_plan (30+30+30+20), traced in 10-tick steps to confirm no ticks are lost to mid-block event interruption at these chunk boundaries. `revolted` stays false throughout (command-mode traced).
Fourth and final chunk — all 4 holes have landed by cumulative +110 ticks post-drill_plan (command-mode traced).
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

expect.note: #553's own drilling-tick block (added post-drill_plan to let the driller finish 4 holes) pushes cumulative ticks well past the ~161 mark the file description notes as when the 5th and final survey (the once-interrupted seismic at 15,15) completes too -- so by this point all 5 of 5 are done, not 4 of 5 as before the drilling block existed.
